Thirteen comments

“Muiris O’ Dalaigh’s”

This tune could also be played with the c’s sharp (^c), which would make it A Mixolydian. Many of the transcriptions I’ve come across for this avoid c altogether…

The most basic transcription I’ve found for this was in this now out-of-print collection of West Kerry music ~

“An Pota Stóir: The Set Dance Music of West Kerry”
Feargal MacAmhlaoibh
INNÉ, County Kerry, 1994
ISBN: 0-9522090-2-0
Page 14, tune #4: “Daliagh’s”

X: 2
T: Dalaigh 2
M: 2/4
L: 1/8
R: polka
K: A Dorian

Dalaigh’s Polka 2

This was the first of two fiddle polkas taught to us by Owen Spafford at Music in the Mountain, Wales, in August 2024.
Owen gave it great feeling and even taught us the Irish style dance to it.
I haven’t put in all the ornaments and variations that were taught to us, just the basic tune which we did mostly in the lower octave, but also in the upper one too. I’ve only written the B part in the upper octave.
I’ve made up the guitar chords for it so they’re not prescriptive…Jan Howard

↳ Posted by Jan Howard on August 25th, 2024.
